summary: Your need for closeness and your fear of it sit on opposite ends of a see-saw, and it plays out through other people. You pull someone close, then feel the cold set in. Or you end up the distant one across the table.
body: Your need for closeness and your fear of it sit on opposite ends of a see-saw, and it plays out through other people. You pull someone close, then feel the cold set in. Or you end up the distant one across the table. Closeness may feel complicated by caution. Part of you may want care, while another part stays alert to distance, conditions, or emotional restraint. Closeness may ask more of you than expected. This can show up as choosing unavailable people, or becoming less available when emotional needs become real. Either way, the gap is the point. Warmth is the harder, braver thing here, and the work is staying in the room when it gets real.
gift: At your best: committed, dependable, the one who actually stays once you decide to.
shadow: The trap: choosing distance and calling it standards, or going cold the second it counts.
integration: Let emotional needs and discipline and limits cooperate without making either one carry the whole story. Dependable under pressure; the risk is grinding joylessly.
do: Stay in the room when it gets close
Notice if you keep picking the unavailable ones
dont: Wait to feel safe before you show up
